thread:
sam (eng-platform): heads up — after the new eu-west1-gpu batch came up (~50 nodes) we saw a 2-3 minute eviction wave and a bunch of pods rescheduled across AZs. a few long-running eval jobs were killed and restarted.

tasha (eng-sre): ugh. did this start immediately after the autoscaler finished adding instances? :eyes:

sam (eng-platform): yeah within ~90s of scale-up completion. symptoms: NodeReady flaps then `kubelet` evicts pods with `grace=0` in some nodes. logs attached inline.

ops-bot: node/drain-triggerer eu-west1-gpu-054 initiated by autoscaler (reason: scaleUpComplete)

jordan (oncall): grabbing kubelet logs & `kubectl describe node` for a few affected nodes now.

jordan (oncall): snippet from kubelet log:

```
I0305 12:24:18.312 kubelet.go:2022] Node not ready: network plugin reports: CNI failed to set up pod "..." network: timed out
I0305 12:24:19.410 eviction_manager.go:312] eviction manager: trying to reclaim ephemeral-storage
I0305 12:24:20.512 eviction_manager.go:428] evicting pod "eval-runner-23" - reason: nodefs.available
```

tasha (eng-sre): that looks like network/CNI races during node bootstrap -> kubelet flips NotReady -> eviction TTL kicks in. Are new nodes using the same kube-proxy/overlay config or a different image/AMIs?

sam (eng-platform): same AMI, but we applied a kube-proxy + cilium config tweak last week (esp. around MTU and iptablesRestore timeout). could be it.

diego (eng-infra): two things we noticed recently: the new GPU pool boots with a tighter `kubelet.evictionHard` (we set `nodefs.available` to 2% to force eviction earlier for noisy local disk workloads), and autoscaler triggers a cluster-level descheduler run right after scale-up. together that can cause coalesced evictions.

diego (eng-infra): suggested immediate mitigations:
- add a temporary taint `node.k8s.redwood/new-node=true:NoSchedule` during first 3m of bootstrap to avoid scheduling heavy eval pods
- relax `evictionHard` for the GPU pool to 1% while we validate image changes
- increase kubelet `node-status-update-frequency` grace on scale events

sam (eng-platform): +1 to taint. we should also avoid running the descheduler immediately after scale-up; it currently rebalances lower-priority pods onto the fresh nodes which then triggers pod churn.

tasha (eng-sre): alternative: mark new nodes `PreferNoSchedule` via pod anti-affinity default, and let the autoscaler backfill lower-priority pods after a 10m cooldown. quick patch to cluster-autoscaler: set `--max-node-provision-time` and add `--ok-to-evict=false` for certain lower-priority RBs.

jordan (oncall): I tested a repro locally: when CNI init exceeds ~45s, kubelet hits readiness flip and pods without tolerations/priority get cleaned up by eviction manager after ~30s. so combined window is small.

sam (eng-platform): we lost some important long-running evals (priority=medium). Cost-wise we prefer packing these into reserved dedicated pools anyway. maybe we should move evals to dedicated-gpu-pool with `priorityClass=high` or pin via nodeSelector.

diego (eng-infra): plan of action I'm going to push in next 30m:
1) add bootstrap taint script into instance-userdata for new GPU pool (3m taint)
2) update GPU pool kubelet config to `evictionHard: { nodefs.available: "1%" }` and increase `eviction-soft` thresholds for disk/network
3) disable immediate descheduler run post-scale (add 10m cooldown)
4) create a quickrun playbook to move low-priority evals to dedicated-gpu-pool (nodeSelector + tolerations)

sam (eng-platform): I'll open a PR for the evals -> dedicated pool migration and add a dashboard alert for 'coalesced evictions' (eviction count spikes per AZ in 5m window).

tasha (eng-sre): also recommend: bump CNI readiness timeout and add `systemd` ready probe in the AMI so node reports `NodeReady` only after CNI is up. that reduces the chance kubelet will mark NotReady while networking still converging.

jordan (oncall): created an incident note and pinned logs: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1934567899 (will include affected node list + restarted pod names). tagging @diego for infra changes.

ops-bot: deploy-trigger eu-west1-gpu-bootstrap-taint commit f9c3a2 queued

diego (eng-infra): pushed taint change, will monitor. if we still see evictions after this, next step is to gate scheduling with kubelet `--register-with-taints` during init.

sam (eng-platform): thanks all. follow-up actions:
- diego: infra changes (taint + eviction adjustments) — in prod in 30m
- sam: move evals PR + dashboard alert
- tasha: AMI/CNI readiness probe changes
- jordan: bind incident notes and postmortem if evictions repeat

sam (eng-platform): low-priority TODO: discuss cost tradeoff (pack vs dedicated) in next infra sync. packing more risks noisy-neighbor evictions; dedicated increases committed spend but reduces churn.

tasha (eng-sre): marking this thread resolved for now. please react with :thumbsup: when monitoring looks stable.

sam (eng-platform): :thumbsup:

jordan (oncall): monitoring stable for last 12m, no new mass-evictions. closing incident at 12:46 UTC.
